page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.7xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by 64.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 33 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX and AVX-512 instruction sets, though it lacks newer extensions like AMX or AVX-512 VNNI. There is no local storage or bundled GPU included with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 29309.22 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8155.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average throughput, reaching 88.67 GB/sec for large block reads. Cryptographic and database operations also perform in the average tier, with Redis SET operations achieving 31.14 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.n1.7xlarge is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2 and its lack of local storage, which requires relying on network-attached storage. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this hardware profile is structured for parallelized workloads that require significant CPU cores but have modest memory requirements. It is suitable for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and parallelized decompression workloads, whereas it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or single-threaded applications.
